item.title: Canadian petition to expel US ambassador gains over 170,000 signatures
item.description: The petition is set to be discussed by House of Commons in a sign of discontent with policies of US President Trump.

item.title: Moroccan Police Intercept Migrants Heading for Ceuta Enclave
item.description: Security forces in Fnideq have stepped up operations to prevent migrants from crossing into Ceuta.

item.title: Moroccan police arrest over 100 migrants trying to reach Spanish enclave
item.description: A social media campaign encouraged people to flock to Ceuta just weeks after many died while making the crossing.

item.title: Death toll from Zimbabwe ferry disaster rises to 72
item.description: Police say 26 more bodies have been recovered from Lake Kariba after the overloaded vessel capsized on Tuesday.

item.title: La Liga: Real Madrid key talking points heading into new 2026-27 season
item.description: Real Madrid welcome back Jose Mourinho as manager as they attempt to stop a three-peat by Barcelona in La Liga.

item.title: Cleanup underway as Russian oil spill reaches Oman’s coastline
item.description: Cleanup crews are responding along 12 kilometres of Omani coastline following an oil spill from the grounded tanker.

item.title: US aircraft carrier expected to relieve USS Lincoln in Middle East
item.description: The USS Washington's movement comes amid reports of dire conditions on the USS Lincoln amid the ongoing Iran war.

item.title: Inter Milan sign England’s Djed Spence from Tottenham Hotspur
item.description: The 26-year-old, who has signed a five-year deal, cost the Italian champions about $40m, according to media reports.

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala expected to strengthen as it nears Hawaii
item.description: Authorities warn residents to take precautions as storm expected to bring rain and strong winds to the island chain.

item.title: UK PM Burnham reacts to death of former Cambridge professor
item.description: Jason Arday was found dead on Friday, just days after resigning amid intense scrutiny over his academic work.

item.title: Erdogan says Egypt could join Turkiye-Saudi-Pakistan defence pact
item.description: Turkish president tells Al Jazeera that the recently signed agreement is open to new members as he pledges continued support.

item.title: One killed, dozens injured after wildfire hits Croatian coast
item.description: At least one person was killed and around 42 others were injured after a violent wildfire hit a coastal town in Croatia.

item.title: Sudan’s al-Burhan pledges immunity for dialogue, rules out Hemedti return
item.description: Al-Burhan pledged temporary immunity and legal protections for participants in a Sudanese national dialogue.

item.title: Ukraine hits Russian Starlink-style network, Moscow tracks arms package
item.description: Ukraine used domestically produced Flamingo missiles to hit targets in Russia's southwestern Samara region.

item.title: Israeli settlers besiege Palestinian families in occupied West Bank
item.description: Three Palestinian families say they have been trapped inside their homes in the occupied West Bank for nearly a week.

item.title: Sedition to anthem: Many lives of ‘Azadi’ chants in India’s youth protests
item.description: A decade ago, student leaders were jailed for shouting 'Azadi', which means freedom.

item.title: How blind football is helping women overcome barriers in Mexico
item.description: Mexico is sending its first blind women's football team to compete in an international tournament. Players cannot wait.

item.title: The next Yemen war might be different
item.description: Drones are no longer the advantage for only one side.

item.title: Afghans mark five years of Taliban rule
item.description: Afghans have gathered in Kabul to mark five years since the Taliban returned to power.

item.title: Black professor at centre of Cambridge plagiarism row found dead
item.description: Dr Jason Arday has been found dead days after resigning from Cambridge University due to plagiarism allegations.

item.title: Vienna woman sues city for discrimination over toilet fees
item.description: An Austrian activist in Vienna is challenging the city over public toilet fees.

item.title: Five wounded in shooting at Virginia State University, multiple suspects
item.description: Police found the gunshot victims near the US university's halls of residence.

item.title: Five years on, how will Taliban deal with armed opposition?
item.description: The United Nations says armed groups opposed to the government remain active.

item.title: Afghan refugees face an uncertain future as Europe shifts to the right
item.description: With the fall of the former government in Kabul, thousands of Afghans were forced to flee the country, many to Europe.

item.title: Is China seeking to copy Iran’s Strait of Hormuz blockade around Taiwan?
item.description: Taiwan has long prepared for a Chinese military invasion but wars in Iran and Ukraine expose new potential threats.
